funFacts: Singapore Grand Prix is the original Formula 1 night race, running under 1,600 floodlights.
Marina Bay has featured at least one safety car in every single edition since its 2008 debut.
Drivers can lose up to three kilograms of body weight during the grueling two-hour race.

headline: Singapore GP: Marina Bay lights ignite as Antonelli leads grid into Thursday track walk
whyCareReason: 1,600 floodlights illuminate Marina Bay as championship leader Kimi Antonelli and title challengers complete Thursday inspections ahead of Friday practice.
teaser: Thursday 1 October: The Marina Bay street circuit lights up in Singapore. Drivers complete track walks and technical press briefings ahead of Friday free practice.
story:
Why this one matters: Thursday evening transformed the Singapore waterfront into a radiant spectacle as 1,600 floodlight projectors illuminated the 4.94-kilometer Marina Bay Street Circuit for Formula 1's premier night race.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli led the Mercedes engineering crew on their formal track walk, examining the newly resurfaced braking zones into turns 7 and 14. Holding an 88-point lead over teammate George Russell, the 19-year-old Italian expressed quiet confidence while acknowledging the oppressive 30-degree Celsius heat and punishing humidity that make Singapore the physical pinnacle of the calendar.

Across the paddock, Ferrari and McLaren revealed substantial high-downforce floor and beam-wing upgrades aimed at challenging Mercedes on the 19-corner layout. With Friday Free Practice 1 and 2 just hours away, every team is dialing in setup data for one of the season's most unpredictable races.
stakes: Antonelli seeks to defend his 88-point cushion while Ferrari and McLaren deploy high-downforce upgrades to close the gap.
rivalryAngle: High-downforce street battle tests Mercedes straight-line superiority against McLaren and Ferrari agility.
